selected_result: Symmetric backward error for a symmetric linear system

bibliographic_source.title: Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms, 2nd ed., Chapter 7: Perturbation Theory for Linear Systems, Problem 7.12

paper_locations.anchor: Problem 7.12: whether a small backward error implies a small symmetric backward error, normwise and componentwise

task_clarification: Let A in R^{n x n} be symmetric and let y be an approximate solution to A x = b.
Formalize: if (A + G) y = b for some G, then there exists a symmetric H = H^T with (A + H) y = b and ||H|| bounded in terms of ||G||.
Treat the normwise case as stated by the source.
The result says a small general backward error implies a comparably small structure-preserving backward error.
scope_constraints: A is symmetric; the perturbed matrix must also be symmetric.
This is an exact perturbation-theoretic statement; no floating-point model is required.
State the norm in which the bound holds explicitly.
Represent the existence claim rather than assuming the symmetric perturbation is given.
